name: Enrolled students
definition: Students enrolled at the school on the October 1 count, by grade and student group
aggregation: sum across schools; never sum grade ALL with grade rows
breaks: Coverage break between 2013-14 and 2014-15: files for 2009-10 to 2013-14 cover district schools only (131,894 students in 2013-14); from 2014-15 they include charter and alternative schools (197,694). Do not draw a trend line across that break without labeling it. 2014-15 to 2018-19 files were reposted in Aug 2025 under new suppression rules. 2010-11 Black, Hispanic, American Indian, and multiracial counts are withheld (zeros in the source; corrections/enrollment.csv).
usage_notes: Groups under the district's threshold are suppressed (2009-10 to 2013-14: whole rows with 20 or fewer students). Economically disadvantaged counts exist only for 2012-13 and 2013-14 and use a different method from the later CEP rate.

name: Economically disadvantaged rate (CEP)
definition: Share of students the district counts as economically disadvantaged under the federal Community Eligibility Provision method
breaks: CEP direct-certification method; not comparable to free/reduced lunch counts from other places
usage_notes: A poverty proxy. Do not use alone to rank or label schools.

name: Students by catchment and school
definition: Students who live in a catchment (by last address on file at the Oct 1 snapshot) and are enrolled at a given school
usage_notes: Catchment 'not available' means the address could not be placed; destinations outside the district list are placeholder schools (cyber and out-of-city charters).

name: Building capacity
definition: Seats the district counts for the school's building
aggregation: sum per building, not per school (co-located schools share a building)
breaks: Facilities planning capacity figures have shifted between releases
usage_notes: Check co-location before comparing; see facilities data gaps.

name: Total enrollment (retention file)
definition: Total students enrolled at the school as reported in the district's catchment retention file
usage_notes: May differ slightly from enrollment_count totals because of snapshot and program rules.

name: Catchment size
definition: Students living in the school's catchment who are enrolled in any public school (district, charter, or cyber)
aggregation: not aggregable across levels (ES, MS, HS catchments overlap)
breaks: Catchment boundaries change by year
usage_notes: Only neighborhood (catchment) schools have catchments.

name: Catchment students attending
definition: Students who live in the school's catchment and attend the school
usage_notes: Numerator of both retention percentages.

name: Enrollment to catchment ratio
definition: School enrollment divided by catchment size
usage_notes: High values can mean a small catchment or many students from elsewhere.

name: Share of catchment students who attend
definition: Catchment students attending the school as a percent of all students living in the catchment
aggregation: recompute from counts; do not average
usage_notes: Denominator is residents, not enrollment. Citywide (sum of attending over sum of catchment size, this project's calculation): 47.4% in 2016-17, 38.1% to 38.8% from 2021-22 to 2025-26.

name: Share of enrollment from the catchment
definition: Catchment students attending the school as a percent of the school's enrollment
aggregation: recompute from counts; do not average
usage_notes: Denominator is the school's enrollment, not catchment residents.

name: Public school students living in the neighborhood (estimate)
definition: Students living in catchments, spread over neighborhoods by where each catchment's 2020 population lives (catchment_flow_to_neighborhood_v1)
aggregation: sum across neighborhoods (not exactly additive to citywide because of unplaced students)
breaks: 2016-17 and 2017-18 have many more students with unplaced addresses (15,735 and 27,911 vs about 2,000 recently), so early estimates undercount
usage_notes: Estimate, not a count. Under 20 is suppressed.

name: Neighborhood students attending their catchment school (estimate)
definition: Of resident students, those enrolled at the school whose catchment they live in (catchment_flow_to_neighborhood_v1)
breaks: 2016-17 and 2017-18 have many more students with unplaced addresses (15,735 and 27,911 vs about 2,000 recently), so early estimates undercount
usage_notes: Estimate. Under 20 is suppressed.

name: Share of neighborhood students attending their catchment school (estimate)
definition: attending_catchment_school_est divided by resident_students_est
breaks: 2016-17 and 2017-18 have many more students with unplaced addresses (15,735 and 27,911 vs about 2,000 recently), so early estimates undercount
usage_notes: Suppressed when the numerator is under 20. Describes family choices and seat availability together; not a measure of school quality.

name: Neighborhood students enrolled in district-run schools (estimate)

breaks: 2016-17 and 2017-18 have many more students with unplaced addresses (15,735 and 27,911 vs about 2,000 recently), so early estimates undercount
usage_notes: Estimate. Under 20 is suppressed. Sector is the school's governance that year, or its most recent listed year.

name: Percent proficient or advanced, ELA/Literature
definition: Share of tested students scoring proficient or advanced on the PSSA English language arts or the Keystone Literature exam
aggregation: recompute from counts; do not average
breaks: No spring 2020 state tests: the 2019-20 file repeats 2018-19 results (status carried_forward). 2020-21 had low participation and no growth scores.
usage_notes: Tracks student poverty closely (r about -0.67 in 2024-25 in the prototype). Read with growth and student-group context; never rank on it alone.

name: Percent proficient or advanced, Mathematics/Algebra 1
definition: Share of tested students scoring proficient or advanced on PSSA math or the Keystone Algebra 1 exam
aggregation: recompute from counts; do not average
breaks: No spring 2020 state tests: the 2019-20 file repeats 2018-19 results (status carried_forward). 2020-21 had low participation and no growth scores.
usage_notes: Same caution as ELA.

name: Percent proficient or advanced, Science/Biology
definition: Share of tested students scoring proficient or advanced on PSSA science or the Keystone Biology exam
aggregation: recompute from counts; do not average
breaks: No spring 2020 state tests: the 2019-20 file repeats 2018-19 results (status carried_forward). 2020-21 had low participation and no growth scores. Science reporting was waived in 2024-25.
usage_notes: Same caution as ELA.

name: Academic growth score, ELA/Literature (PVAAS)
definition: PDE's Future Ready score for meeting annual academic growth expectations in ELA, based on PVAAS
breaks: No spring 2020 state tests: the 2019-20 file repeats 2018-19 results (status carried_forward). 2020-21 had low participation and no growth scores.
usage_notes: Not a percent of students. Fairer to high-poverty schools than proficiency but noisy for a single year; pool years before comparing.

name: Academic growth score, Mathematics/Algebra 1 (PVAAS)
definition: PDE's Future Ready score for meeting annual academic growth expectations in math, based on PVAAS
breaks: No spring 2020 state tests: the 2019-20 file repeats 2018-19 results (status carried_forward). 2020-21 had low participation and no growth scores.
usage_notes: Not a percent of students. More stable year to year than ELA growth; still pool years.

name: Academic growth score, Science/Biology (PVAAS)
definition: PDE's Future Ready score for meeting annual academic growth expectations in science, based on PVAAS
breaks: No spring 2020 state tests: the 2019-20 file repeats 2018-19 results (status carried_forward). 2020-21 had low participation and no growth scores.
usage_notes: Not a percent of students.

name: Test participation, ELA/Literature
definition: Share of eligible students who took the state ELA/Literature test
breaks: No spring 2020 state tests: the 2019-20 file repeats 2018-19 results (status carried_forward). 2020-21 had low participation and no growth scores.
usage_notes: Low participation makes proficiency and growth less reliable.

name: Test participation, Mathematics/Algebra 1
definition: Share of eligible students who took the state math/Algebra 1 test
breaks: No spring 2020 state tests: the 2019-20 file repeats 2018-19 results (status carried_forward). 2020-21 had low participation and no growth scores.
usage_notes: Low participation makes proficiency and growth less reliable.

name: Test participation, Science/Biology
definition: Share of eligible students who took the state science/Biology test
breaks: No spring 2020 state tests: the 2019-20 file repeats 2018-19 results (status carried_forward). 2020-21 had low participation and no growth scores.

name: Grade 3 reading proficiency
definition: Share of grade 3 students proficient or advanced in ELA (Future Ready early indicator)
breaks: No spring 2020 state tests: the 2019-20 file repeats 2018-19 results (status carried_forward). 2020-21 had low participation and no growth scores.

name: Grade 7 math proficiency
definition: Share of grade 7 students proficient or advanced in math (Future Ready early indicator)
breaks: No spring 2020 state tests: the 2019-20 file repeats 2018-19 results (status carried_forward). 2020-21 had low participation and no growth scores.

name: Regular attendance (2017-18 to 2020-21)
definition: Share of students enrolled 90 or more days who attended at least 90% of the days they were enrolled, as PDE defined it before 2021-22
breaks: Renamed and redefined as persistent attendance (pct_persistent_attendance) in 2021-22: do not join the two into one line without marking the break.
usage_notes: Moderately poverty-linked; stable year to year.

name: Persistent attendance (2021-22 on)
definition: PDE's attendance measure from 2021-22 on, which replaced regular attendance
breaks: Replaces pct_regular_attendance; definitions differ, so mark the break on any trend.
usage_notes: Check PDE's current definition before comparing with other states.

name: Chronic absenteeism
definition: Share of students absent 10% or more of the days they were enrolled
breaks: First published in the 2024-25 Future Ready file.

name: Four-year graduation rate
definition: Share of the cohort that graduated within four years
breaks: Cohort definitions follow PDE; the reported year is the graduation year.
usage_notes: High schools only.

name: Five-year graduation rate
definition: Share of the cohort that graduated within five years
usage_notes: High schools only.

name: Students tested (district PSSA/Keystone)
definition: Students with a score on the test, by school, grade, subject, and group (district 'Actual' files: all tested students)
breaks: 2014-15: PSSA replaced by tests aligned to Pennsylvania Core standards (Reading became ELA; Writing dropped) and proficiency fell sharply (grades 3-8 math 46.9% to 17.8% citywide); never draw one line across it. 2011-12: grades 3-8 proficiency fell about 8 points citywide; check the cause before attributing it. No 2019-20 or 2020-21 district files. Keystone exams replaced grade 11 PSSA from 2012-13.
usage_notes: District schools only; charter results are in school_metric from Future Ready.

name: Students at a performance level (district PSSA/Keystone)
definition: Students scoring below basic, basic, proficient, advanced, or proficient or advanced
breaks: 2014-15: PSSA replaced by tests aligned to Pennsylvania Core standards (Reading became ELA; Writing dropped) and proficiency fell sharply (grades 3-8 math 46.9% to 17.8% citywide); never draw one line across it. 2011-12: grades 3-8 proficiency fell about 8 points citywide; check the cause before attributing it. No 2019-20 or 2020-21 district files. Keystone exams replaced grade 11 PSSA from 2012-13.
usage_notes: Recompute shares from counts rather than averaging percents.

name: Percent at a performance level (district PSSA/Keystone)
definition: Share of tested students at each performance level; stored 0 to 100 (older files used fractions and were rescaled)
aggregation: recompute from counts; do not average
breaks: 2014-15: PSSA replaced by tests aligned to Pennsylvania Core standards (Reading became ELA; Writing dropped) and proficiency fell sharply (grades 3-8 math 46.9% to 17.8% citywide); never draw one line across it. 2011-12: grades 3-8 proficiency fell about 8 points citywide; check the cause before attributing it. No 2019-20 or 2020-21 district files. Keystone exams replaced grade 11 PSSA from 2012-13.
usage_notes: Matches Future Ready ELA proficiency at r = 0.996 (2018-19) for schools in both. Read with poverty and growth; never rank on it.

name: Enrollment (state Fast Facts)
definition: Students enrolled at the school as reported by PDE in School Fast Facts
usage_notes: State count; may differ from the district's October 1 count (enrollment_count) because of snapshot date and program rules. Covers district and charter schools on one definition.

name: Share of enrollment by student group (state Fast Facts)
definition: Percent of the school's students in the group (student_group): economically disadvantaged, English learner, special education, gifted, homeless, foster care, military-connected, female, male, or a race/ethnicity group
breaks: Foster care is blank in 2024-25; gifted is reported as zero for many schools that may simply not report it.
usage_notes: Economically disadvantaged uses PDE's definition, not the district's CEP rate; do not mix the two in one trend.

name: Comparison with poverty peers
definition: A school's result next to the 15 non-selective schools in its grade band with the closest student poverty share: peer median, peer middle half (25th-75th percentile), difference from the peer median, and position (above, within, or below the peer range). Columns of derived/peer_comparison; method poverty_peers_k15_v1
breaks: Census bases switch ACS period between 2019-20 and 2020-21. Student-poverty basis has almost no 2017-18 district comparisons (the state file leaves the figure blank for district schools).
usage_notes: Facts, not rankings: never sort schools by it or combine it into a score. Three poverty bases side by side (school students' state econ disadvantaged share; ACS child poverty of the school's catchment; enrollment-weighted ACS child poverty where the school's students live). The basis changes the position for about half of schools, so show bases together. Positions repeat only moderately across non-overlapping periods (r 0.60 proficiency, 0.34-0.45 growth). Selective-admission schools are not compared.

name: People in poverty (ACS)
definition: Share of people for whom poverty status is determined whose income is below the poverty level (B17001)
breaks: Two ACS periods: 2015-2019 (2010 tracts, crosswalked through 2020 blocks by 2020 population) and 2020-2024 (2020 tracts). Peer comparisons use 2015-2019 for school years through 2019-20 and 2020-2024 after. Income is in each period's own dollars (2019 or 2024): adjust for inflation before comparing.
usage_notes: Citywide 21.4% (2020-2024). Rollups to catchments, zones, and neighborhoods allocate tract counts by 2020 population share; no margin of error for rollups yet.

name: Children in poverty (ACS)
definition: Share of children under 18 (poverty status determined) below the poverty level (B17001 under-18 lines)
breaks: Two ACS periods: 2015-2019 (2010 tracts, crosswalked through 2020 blocks by 2020 population) and 2020-2024 (2020 tracts). Peer comparisons use 2015-2019 for school years through 2019-20 and 2020-2024 after. Income is in each period's own dollars (2019 or 2024): adjust for inflation before comparing.
usage_notes: Citywide 29.0%. Used as the census basis in peer comparison.

name: Adults with a bachelor's degree or more (ACS)
definition: Share of people 25 and over with a bachelor's, master's, professional, or doctorate degree (B15003)
breaks: Two ACS periods: 2015-2019 (2010 tracts, crosswalked through 2020 blocks by 2020 population) and 2020-2024 (2020 tracts). Peer comparisons use 2015-2019 for school years through 2019-20 and 2020-2024 after. Income is in each period's own dollars (2019 or 2024): adjust for inflation before comparing.
usage_notes: Citywide 35.4%.

name: Owner-occupied homes (ACS)
definition: Share of occupied housing units that are owner occupied (B25003)
breaks: Two ACS periods: 2015-2019 (2010 tracts, crosswalked through 2020 blocks by 2020 population) and 2020-2024 (2020 tracts). Peer comparisons use 2015-2019 for school years through 2019-20 and 2020-2024 after. Income is in each period's own dollars (2019 or 2024): adjust for inflation before comparing.
usage_notes: Citywide 51.8%. Rollups weight by population, not households (approximation).

name: Median household income (ACS, tract)
definition: Median household income in the past 12 months, 2024 dollars (B19013), with margin of error
breaks: Two ACS periods: 2015-2019 (2010 tracts, crosswalked through 2020 blocks by 2020 population) and 2020-2024 (2020 tracts). Peer comparisons use 2015-2019 for school years through 2019-20 and 2020-2024 after. Income is in each period's own dollars (2019 or 2024): adjust for inflation before comparing.
usage_notes: Tract only; see the _approx measure for larger areas.

name: Median household income, approximate (ACS rollup)
definition: Household-weighted average of tract median incomes for a catchment, zone, or neighborhood
breaks: Two ACS periods: 2015-2019 (2010 tracts, crosswalked through 2020 blocks by 2020 population) and 2020-2024 (2020 tracts). Peer comparisons use 2015-2019 for school years through 2019-20 and 2020-2024 after. Income is in each period's own dollars (2019 or 2024): adjust for inflation before comparing.
usage_notes: Not a true median; label it as approximate.
